title.value: Contextual bandit optimization of super-resolution microscopy
title.justification: The title 'Contextual bandit optimization of super-resolution microscopy' correctly captures the central theme of the paper which involves optimizing imaging parameters in super-resolution microscopy using contextual bandit algorithms.
title.quote: Contextual bandit optimization of super-resolution microscopy

extractions.description: This paper explores the optimization of imaging parameters in super-resolution microscopy using contextual bandit algorithms. It frames the task as an optimization problem, focusing on the trade-offs between objectives such as spatio-temporal resolution, signal-to-noise ratio, and photobleaching. It employs structured actions in a contextual bandit framework to identify sample-dependent imaging parameters.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: While the paper is focused on optimization in microscopy, which could have indirect implications for sustainable development in terms of improving research efficiency and outcomes, it does not directly address themes related to Climate or Ecologically-Related Sustainable Development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: The optimization of the thresholds of DyMIN were tackled as a use case since they should vary as a function of available knowledge, i.e. the intensity of the sample. Using the contextual information, the models could modify their parameters dependant on the experimental conditions and outperform their counterpart blindly trained.

primary_category.justification: The paper focuses on the optimization of imaging parameters in super-resolution microscopy and does not align directly with any specific Climate or Ecologically-Related Sustainable Development categories listed.
primary_category.quote: In this work, we frame the optimization problem as a multi-armed bandit framework with contextual information about the sample to identify optimal sample-dependant imaging parameters.

secondary_categories.justification: The study does not directly engage with multiple sustainable development themes, focusing instead on technical optimization in microscopy.
secondary_categories.quote: This framework has been extensively studied in the literature and applied to recommendation systems and medical treatment planning.

primary_sub_category.justification: No sub-category directly related to Climate or Ecologically-Related Sustainable Development is addressed, as the paper's focus is on microscopy.
primary_sub_category.quote: We frame the problem of selecting the DyMIN parameters based on the state of the current sample as a contextual bandit problem.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The focus remains on technical advancements in microscopy without engaging with specific sub-categories related to sustainable development.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: We define two DyMIN thresholds as the parameters to be optimized.

applications.value: Optimization of imaging parameters in super-resolution microscopy
applications.justification: This application is the main focus of the study, which aims to improve the resolution and efficiency of imaging in microscopy through contextual bandit optimization.
applications.quote: The online optimization of optical microscopy parameters aims at learning the set of imaging parameters while the experiment unfolds.

new_primary_category.justification: The research does not present a new Climate or Ecological-Related Sustainable Development category, as its focus is on technical optimization in microscopy.
new_primary_category.quote: We build on existing work by formulating the optimization problem of sample-dependant parameters as a contextual bandit problem with structured actions.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not introduce new sub-categories related to sustainable development; its contributions lie in the field of technical optimization.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: This approach considered one regression model per objective to induce a notion of structure onto the set of possible actions.
